role: camera block (E61 V3-DTF tier 2, plan section 10)

tier2_primary.hi_minus_lo_caveat: hi ran before lo in ALL FOUR passes, so the lo arm carries the preceding hi block's residual heat and hi_minus_lo is biased. On the cross-checker's synthetic hi-first campaign the tool read hi_minus_lo = +61.95 mK against a planted +35.8 mK (a 73% overstatement) while reading hi itself exactly. Read hi as the statistic; hi_minus_lo is an upper bound.

tier2_spatial.mm_note: the camera was never calibrated on this card and the automatic bbox is the whole frame, not the card, so no mm scale is established and the plan's '~11 mm' prediction is NOT testable from this block. The identified quantities are the monopole, the gradient and its direction, and the profile in pixels.

orthogonal_axis.what: the same reduction with the frame halved across y instead of x
orthogonal_axis.reads: no effect; the signal lives on the x axis alone

die_footprint_rects.what: patches restricted to the mean frame's 2nd Otsu level, x 25..211, y 3..184 (label-blind), cut at the same x = 128
die_footprint_rects.reads: the statistic survives dropping the frame's outer border

hi.note: the side term is what the reduction reports as T; the order term is how much the statistic depends on WHICH side ran first, which the W-first/E-first alternation makes orthogonal to it. An artefact of the block order lives entirely in the order term, so a large side term with a small order term is the signature of a real side effect. The t is a parametric side-note on 2 df, NOT the registered inference -- that is the permutation p.

controls.lo_carryover_detector: the tool's own check (lo gradient opposed to hi by >120 deg and not small) did NOT fire: lo points at +172.9 deg against hi's +173.8 deg, the same way. The lo arm is a real lower-amplitude copy of the same contrast, not an inverted control.

geometry.why_it_was_kept: Otsu's largest component covers 85.6% of the frame and its bbox is the whole frame, so the mask is the warm board, not the card -- the tool's own warning fired. It was kept as the PRIMARY anyway because the geometry it produces is right: the frame halved across its longer axis cuts at x = 128, and the mean difference image's own neutral band sits at x = 129, one pixel away. The die-footprint rectangles are reported beside it as the sensitivity arm.

tier1_board_meter.source: the dtf-cam block's own telemetry.jsonl.gz, board_w at 10 Hz, ~416 samples per item per pass
tier1_board_meter.registered_rule: E-D7 tier 1 (README section 9, row C58 C83 C84 C91): board power for d7w_hi and d7e_hi equal within 3 SE. This block is NOT the registered family-B half-die amplitude arm, which is measured on the pinned 600 MHz card; this is the same equality test read on the dtf-cam block's own meter at aifoundry2's 800 MHz / 0.618 V.
tier1_board_meter.reading: Taken as the registered statistic reads literally -- the pass as the unit of replication, no order term -- hi is EQUAL within 3 SE (|t| 1.43) and lo already DIFFERS (|t| 5.20). But the hi per-pass values track the pass parity (-1.02, +0.16, -0.90, +0.02): the block that runs SECOND reads +0.52 W higher, which inflates the naive SE sixfold. With that balanced order term fitted, the point estimate is unchanged at -0.44 W and |t| is 9.55 -- the two MESH halves are NOT electrically symmetric, by about 0.4 W out of the 12.5-14.4 W the work itself draws (~3%). This is a CROSS-CHECK on this card, not the registered tier-1 arm, which is family B on the pinned 600 MHz card.
caveats: one meter reading per 100 ms, averaged over each run window; no idle rung was run inside dtf-cam, so the 'gap' column is the inter-run wait (the card is between launches, not idle)
the hi blocks precede the lo blocks in all four passes, so hi - lo carries the pass's own time trend; the W-vs-E tests do not, because the side order alternates between passes

verdict.tier: 2 (exploratory by design -- plan section 10 and section 2's E-D7 row carry no CONFIRMED/REFUTED arm)
what_is_established: The pattern MOVES. Swapping which MESH half runs loud moves heat across the board by +372.9 mK on the double difference, p = 0.0007 against the registered cyclic null with all 10,000 labellings enumerated. The hub's prescribed regulator control is PASSED: two fixed voltage regulators cannot produce a pattern that changes sides with the shire mask.
It is a dipole, not a level shift. The card-mean of the difference image (the camera's own read of 'Delta P_card == 0') is -13.2 mK against a +373 mK half-to-half contrast, p = 0.96.
It lies on one axis. Halving the frame the other way returns -11.7 mK, p = 0.29.

It is not the block order. Decomposed on the balanced 2x2, the side term is +372.9 mK and the order term +23.6 mK; once the order term is out the four passes agree to within +/-2.3 mK (SE 1.16 mK on 2 df).
The hart activity alone already carries it: the quiet lo arm shows the same dipole in the same direction (173 deg vs 174 deg) at +202.8 mK, 54% of the loud arm's.
what_is_NOT_established: Which image half is the die's West. The camera's orientation relative to the MESH x<=2 split was never measured, so the finding is 'the image half at lower x heats when the 0x3131733b mask runs' -- label-blind, exactly as the tool's own sign_note says.

Any displacement in millimetres. No mm/px scale exists for this card, and from W-E alone a displacement is not identified in the first place (plan section 10, rule 8). The plan's '~11 mm' is untestable from this block.
Absolute mK, mK/W, or a die-side amplitude: the camera has never been calibrated on this card and the die-to-back coupling is unmeasured (plan section 10, 'what tier 2 cannot show' iii, iv).

The shire map. That the pattern splits where MESH says it should is consistent with the hart->shire->position map, but the halves-only resolution cannot test a single shire (section 10, ii), and the monopole's null SD of 216 mK is far too wide to resolve the 0.44 W electrical asymmetry the board meter does see (~34 mK expected).
Anything at constant TOTAL power. Both arms run half the chip idle, so this is a contrast at constant WORK, not the page's constant-total-power dipole (section 10, i).
verdict.honest_reading: For an exploratory test this is about as clean as it gets: the effect is 2.8 null-SDs out on the conservative cyclic null and sits at or near the floor of the two other nulls, it reproduces in all four passes with an order-adjusted spread of +/-2.3 mK, it survives every assignment, warmup and detrend arm (+349 to +572 mK), it disappears on the orthogonal axis, and the monopole it leaves behind is consistent with zero. The 4-pass block null cannot resolve below p = 0.176 and says so. The one thing to hold loosely is hi_minus_lo: the arm order was not alternated, so that number is an upper bound on the result-path contribution. Nothing here reaches the page's E-D7 as written, and tier 2 was never allowed to.

provenance.frames: rsync of aifoundry2:claude/et-soc1-prototyping/build/dtf-cam (230 MB, 614 frames of 393,216 B each, 0 fetch failures); every frame fell inside a block span, so all 614 are in the primary arm
provenance.disclosure: the geometry decision was taken from the mean frame and the hi-minus-lo level image, both blind to the W/E labels, as rule 5 requires. The W-E difference panels were also viewed before the primary was finalised -- which is why the PRIMARY was left as the tool's own automatic geometry, chosen by the registered rule and not by me; the die-footprint rectangles are reported only as a sensitivity arm, and no p-value was read before the geometry was fixed.
provenance.perms_note: the registered default is 5000 sampled cyclic labellings (p = 0.0012); the primary quoted here enumerates all 10,000 (p = 0.0007). Both are reported.
